# Independent audit: globally critical original-row root Jensen obstruction



Source: `candidate c323819a201d7580`.
Verifier: `supporting computation verify_globally_critical_original_kkt_row_counterexample_simplex_chains.py`.


rational checks. The proof, including the all-normal depth and entire
critical-menu classification, does not rely on that finite check.

## 1. Actual fibers and exact depth

The integer-support argument is exact: an integer point of the projected
hull outside the binary cube has some coordinate -1, and attaining that
coordinate forces its entire convex weight onto v_-. Thus no extra
integer bases are omitted. Each original cube fiber is exactly T, since
it already contains T and every generator lies in T. The extreme extra
fiber is exactly epsilon T. The threshold rho_d is at most its value
in a canonical direction, ((d-1)/(d+1))^d<1, so the assumed smallness
does ensure epsilon<1 and containment in T.

I independently read the cited tiny-endpoint profile proof. For each
continuous direction, the coupled two-endpoint mass is at least
min(a,q(u)), and f(u)-gamma+q(u)>=rho_d>a. This gives the all-halfspace
lower bound gamma+a on the actual three-fiber subset v_-,0,v_+.
The restriction of every ambient integer normal to this line is one
scalar affine tilt, so the argument applies in the larger integer
dimension without changing its constants. Pure-integer boundary mass
is treated separately and exceeds the claimed depth.

The displayed isolating caps give the exact upper bound at the source.
They also give uniqueness: at x!=g in the zero fiber, raise one canonical
threshold to lambda_i(x)>1/(d+1), retaining all of A and excluding the
other cube fibers, to obtain mass strictly below gamma+a. At any other
cube base the isolated canonical cover has budget gamma. At v_- an
exposing pure-integer cap has mass a. Hence the deepest point is exactly
the asserted single actual point (0,g).

The parity and nonheavy calculations are literal: k=2^n and
1<(2^n+a)/2^n. The strict OC excess is
a(1-gamma/2^n)>0, so the example meets no below-target premise.

## 2. Cover and residual optimum

All isolating affine function values in (5)--(6) have the stated signs.
In particular delta_w(v_-)=(2n+3)r-n>=n+3 for a nonzero cube vertex
with r ones. Every own canonical cap has volume gamma and all unwanted
full-dimensional traces are strictly absent. This proves the exact
obstacle vector (0,c,...,c), with c=(1-gamma)^(1/d).

The midpoint relation v_-+v_+=0 gives h_-+h_+>=2h_0>=2c. Convexity
of the power d, with d>=2 and all h nonnegative, gives the lower bound
2c^d on those two terms. Adding the remaining cube obstacles proves
the exact objective value. Strict convexity and the remaining obstacle
equalities force every sampled height to equal c. The support slopes
need not be unique, and the source correctly claims uniqueness only
for the sampled optimal values.

## 3. KKT data and its actual canonical coupling

With s=d c^(d-1), each of the n+1 outgoing source edges has multiplier
s. Their displacement sum v_-+sum e_j is zero. Source stationarity
is (n+2)s=s+(n+1)s, each destination has multiplier zero because its
incoming flow is s, and every remaining base has obstacle multiplier
s. Every support inequality is tight at the constant heights; every
positive obstacle multiplier is at a genuine obstacle contact.

The absorbing chain has no successive nonzero transitions: all
destinations immediately stop. Its exact source terminal row is
uniform on {0,v_-,e_1,...,e_n}, with n+2 atoms. The displayed pi has
the right marginals and barycentric rows, so the violating row is
indeed the canonical coupling of these exact KKT data, not an
arbitrarily chosen feasible measure.

## 4. Every critical cap, not just the displayed isolating ones

Equality of full cap mass with gamma+a forces equality on the three
selected fibers and zero volume on every remaining cube fiber. The
strict rho_d>a profile inequality rules out q(u)<a; in the other case
equality forces f(u)=gamma. The ordinary simplex equality case gives
precisely a canonical continuous normal.

The condition c<n/(n+1) implies n>=2: gamma<1/2 for d>=2, hence
c>1/2, so n=1 cannot qualify. Therefore each unit vertex e_j lies
outside {v_-,0,v_+}. Its trace has zero volume, forcing
beta_j<=-d/(d+1). Conversely those inequalities exclude all nonzero
cube traces in volume, capture all of A because the v_- threshold is
strictly negative, and yield the exact own canonical cap. At equality
an unwanted cube trace can be a single vertex, correctly retained as
a zero-volume closed boundary trace.

Thus the entire critical menu has residual roots (0,c,1,...,1) on the
same terminal row. The strict mean gap is

    [n-(n+1)c]/(n+2)>0.

This is independent of the small endpoint volume a. Adding a critical
cap preserves the old cover and obstacles. Replacing one by a cap in
the same canonical direction preserves the cover; the source correctly
does not claim this after discarding a different canonical direction.

## 5. Dimension condition and exact instance

For n=3d, Bernoulli gives (n/(n+1))^d>1-d/(n+1)>2/3, while the
elementary exponential-series bound gives gamma>1/3. This proves the
required condition in every d>=2 without finite-dimensional sampling.

For d=2,n=3, epsilon=1/10, the profile condition reduces to the exact
rational square comparison in the source. The inequality c<3/4 is
80<81. The displayed Q, M, OC excess17/1800, residual objective5,
and row gap (9-4sqrt(5))/15 all check exactly. The rational-coordinate
and boundary qualifications are accurate.

## 6. Scope

The result disproves the universal assertion that unchanged residual-root
Jensen holds for every valid original KKT row under these unconditional
geometric and criticality assumptions: the given valid row fails for
every choice from its complete critical-cap menu. It does not rule out selecting
different KKT multipliers, and it does not satisfy a below-target
condition. No correction to the source was needed.
